Shared laws, commands and teaching applying to all within the stated audience or conditions. General does not remove covenant, historical, priestly or household limits. Read the existing Transformed, Fulfilled, Unchanged, Everlasting and other classifications alongside each entry.

Some source records still need their audience resolved. These are explicitly marked audience review pending; their provisional filing here is not a claim that they apply universally. Passage groups may contain both shared teaching and personal directions.

General · Personal · Instructions overview

3,869 study records in this view. Entries can overlap; this is not a count of distinct biblical commands. Ordered by the first source book, chapter and verse.

The source wording follows the Saints Greek-English text: the Septuagint for the Old Testament and the Greek New Testament. Headings and application notes are study summaries. Preserve the passage’s speaker, audience, conditions and grammatical form. Source alignment checked 6 November 2026; independent critical-Greek review remains in progress.

C0521 · Priest: inspect and classify the house lesion by the stated criteria

Source wording · Saints Greek-English

14:36 And the priest shall command that the house be emptied before he enters to examine the lesion, so that nothing in the house becomes unclean. Afterward the priest shall enter to examine the house.

14:37 And he shall examine the lesion in the walls of the house, greenish or fiery-red hollows whose appearance is lower than the walls,

14:38 and the priest shall leave the house, go to its door, and isolate the house for seven days.

14:39 And the priest shall return on the seventh day, and examine the house; and, behold, if the lesion has not spread in the walls of the house,

Leviticus 14:36–39

14:44 then the priest shall enter and examine it. If the lesion has spread in the house, it is persistent leprosy in the house; it is unclean.

Leviticus 14:44

14:48 But if the priest comes and enters and examines it, and, behold, the lesion has not spread at all in the house after the house was plastered, the priest shall declare the house clean, for the lesion has healed.

Leviticus 14:48

C0533 · Apply the stated uncleanness periods and contact rules for bodily discharges

Source wording · Saints Greek-English

15:2 Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: If any man has a flow from his body, his flow is unclean.

15:3 And this is the law of his uncleanness: discharging seed from his body through the flow by which his body has become stopped up, this is his uncleanness in him; all the days of the flow of his body, in which his body has become stopped up through the flow, are his uncleanness.

15:4 Every bed on which the man with a seminal discharge lies is unclean, and every article on which the man with a seminal discharge sits shall be unclean.

Leviticus 15:2–4

15:9 And any donkey saddle on which the man with a seminal discharge mounts shall be unclean until evening.

Leviticus 15:9

15:19 And if a woman has a flow of blood, her flow shall be in her body; she shall remain in her menstrual discharge for seven days. Whosoever touches her shall be unclean until evening,

15:20 and everything on which she lies during her menstrual discharge shall be unclean, and everything on which she sits shall be unclean.

Leviticus 15:19–20

15:24 If anyone lies with her and her uncleanness comes upon him, he shall be unclean for seven days, and every bed on which he lies shall be unclean.

15:25 And if a woman has a flow of blood for many days outside the time of her menstrual discharge, or if she also has a flow after her menstrual discharge, all the days of her unclean flow shall be like the days of her menstrual discharge; she shall be unclean.

15:26 And every bed on which she lies during all the days of her flow shall be like the bed of her menstrual discharge, and every article on which she sits shall be unclean, as in the uncleanness of her menstrual discharge.

Leviticus 15:24–26

15:23 If, while she is on her bed or on the article on which she sits, he touches her, he shall be unclean until evening.

Leviticus 15:23
